title: Site area merit assessment criteria
text: M4.1.1 Development of the type and density indicated by the density code designated in the scheme. M4.1.2 The WAPC, in consultation with the local government, may approve the creation of a green title lot or survey-strata lot (excluding battleaxe lots) with a minimum and/or average site area up to 5 per cent less than that specified in Table 2B where it will: i. not create more than one lot with a reduced minimum lots size; ii. facilitate the protection of an environmental or heritage feature; iii. facilitate the retention of a significant element that contributes toward an existing streetscape worthy of retention; iv. facilitate the development of lots with separate and sufficient frontage to more than one public street; v. overcome a special or unusual limitation on the development of the land imposed by its size, shape or other feature; vi. allow land to be developed with housing of the same type and form as land in the vicinity and which would not otherwise be able to be developed; or vii. achieve specific objectives of the local planning framework. M4.1.3 In addition to M4.1.2, the WAPC, in consultation with the local government, may approve any average lot size variation greater than five percent than that specified in Table 2B for R10 to R35 lots (base code applied for dual coded land and excludes battleaxe lots), provided that: i. the site is a corner lot with frontage to two different streets or any other lot with frontage to more than one dedicated street (excluding a primary (red), other regional (blue) or any other major road, including state and federal highways, with access restrictions); ii. all proposed lots comply with the minimum lot size and frontage provision specified in Table 2B; iii. the width and frontage of the new lots will enable dwellings to have their primary frontage to the different streets; iv. crossovers and driveways to proposed lots are provided in accordance with Australian Standard (AS) 2890 and C3.7 Access; and v. any corner truncation, pedestrian access way, vehicle right of way or laneway widening is excluded from the calculation of the minimum lot size. M4.1.4 Potential change: New provision to allow for greater subdivision potential on corner lots coded R10-R17.5. Refer to Information Sheet 5: Lot size and density. M4.1.5 Potential change: New provision to allow minimum site area to be reduced up to 10 per cent where the existing dwelling is retained. Refer to Information Sheet 5: Lot size and density.

notes: Merit criteria of element 4.1 (pages 49-50). M4.1.2-M4.1.5 are WAPC/merit matters, also recorded one per file under rules/4.1 as judgment rules in column M (register ch2-090 to ch2-093). M4.1.4 and M4.1.5 are flagged potential changes with no operative text.
